sources.title: alibaba/open-code-review — README
sources.body: Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. `ocr scan` reviews entire files. Description: Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible. Benchmark: Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), achieves significantly higher Precision and F1 with the same underlying model, while consuming only ~1/9 of the tokens; Recall is lower — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise. Install: npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review. License Apache-2.0.

sources.title: stablyai/orca — README
sources.body: Orca is the ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent with your own subscription. Run Codex, ClaudeCode, OpenCode or Pi side-by-side — each in its own worktree, tracked in one place. Parallel Worktrees: Fan one prompt across five agents, each in its own isolated git worktree — compare the results and merge the winner. Mobile Companion (iOS App Store, Android APK). SSH Worktrees. Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux. License badge: MIT.

sources.title: JustVugg/colibri — README
sources.body: Run frontier MoE models — 744B to 2.8T parameters — on consumer and heterogeneous hardware, in pure C with zero engine dependencies, by treating storage, RAM, and VRAM as a single inference hierarchy. Nine families run today: GLM-5.2/5.3 (744B), GLM-5.3-Flash, Inkling (975B), Kimi K3 (2.8T), DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3.6 (35B-A3B), OLMoE (7B). A 744B MoE model activates only ~40B parameters per token. GLM-5.2: ~372 GB on disk, RAM 16 GB min / 24 GB comfortable, GPU not needed. Measured: 6× RTX 5090 full residency 5.8–6.8 tok/s decode; 128 GB CPU-only desktop ~1.8 tok/s warm; 25 GB dev box 0.05–0.1 tok/s cold. License Apache 2.0.

sources.title: convaiinnovations/laya — model card
sources.body: Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision model. Give it a state (text, email, ticket, or JSON) and typed questions; it returns typed answers with mathematically calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass (~33 ms) across 100+ languages. Trained with RLCD (reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules). It never generates text. Root checkpoint: ModernBERT-large backbone, 421M, context 512, English (guardrails, email triage); laya-multilingual: mmBERT-base 322M, 100+ languages. Fine-tuned laya-typed-decisions scores 0.766 accuracy vs 0.362 for base English checkpoint (2,000 decisions across four workflows). License apache-2.0. sources.title: moondream/parakeet-redux — model card
sources.body: A 1.58-bit version of parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3. Same architecture, same tokenizer, but every encoder weight is -1, 0 or +1. It fits in 178 MB, runs at 113× real time on eight x86 CPU cores, 2.5× the fastest other Parakeet runtime we measured, and stays within 0.3 WER of the original on English while beating it on the 25-language FLEURS set and on long-form audio. Open ASR Leaderboard 7 English sets WER 6.26(original) vs 6.55; FLEURS 25 languages 11.62 vs 10.56; background noise 6.72 vs 9.04; weights 1.2 GB vs 178 MB. Apple M2 MacBook Air CPU 38×. Languages: en, de, fr, es, it, pt, ru, uk ... (25 European languages, Korean not listed). Run with Photon (pip install moondream). License cc-by-4.0. HF API(2026-09-25): createdAt 2026-09-18, trendingScore 147, downloads 918.

sources.title: Qwen/RecreationBench — dataset card
sources.body: RecreationBench is a benchmark of 250 application-recreation tasks across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android, and Web (50 tasks per platform). Held-out evaluation suite of RecreationWorld, a framework for scalable and verifiable environments for hybrid computer-use agents. Given a recreation request and interactive access to a running reference application, an agent explores its behavior, implements a new application, and verifies its own result. Metrics: Prog (reference-grounded programmatic checks) and VLM (visual checks by a VLM judge); macro-averaged per platform then equally weighted across five. Multi-license collection; execution framework MIT. Paper arXiv 2609.22000. HF API(2026-09-25): createdAt 2026-09-18, trendingScore 12, downloads 4,233.
